children: Endeavour Silver's cornerstone silver mine in Mexico has temporarily scaled back capacity after a mechanical problem affecting the primary ball mill.
The Canadian silver producer said the mill at the Guanacevi mine was taken offline on Monday while preparations are completed to replace parts that are available on-site.

The company expects repairs to be completed within about three weeks, during which time the regrind circuit will be configured to operate at a reduced throughput of 600 metric tons a day, compared with the usual about 1,100 tons daily.
Mining operations will continue uninterrupted and Endeavour said the cost of replacing the affected components is expected to be minimal.

Guanacevi is Endeavour's first and highest-grade silver mine, bought by the company in 2004. The mine has produced more than 60 million ounces of silver over 20 years, including 3.92 million ounces in 2025.
